dates.display: 12 November 1661 (the marriage record read as Gurney)

incoming.explanation: The fair-copy manuscript's ink reading 'John Girny, Senior,' with 'Cheny' only a later pencil margin note, is the primary evidence that the record is Gurney.
Pope's independent 1900 records-based ruling that the printed 'John Cheny' is a typographical error corroborates the Gurney reading.

outgoing.explanation: The reading finding reinterprets the printed 'Cheny' surname: it is a later pencil annotation the 1886 print followed, not the fair copy's ink, which reads Girny.
The resolved town-record reading corroborates the (independently attested) second marriage to Grizzell.
The resolved reading confirms the 20 September 1661 'wife of John' death line is Mary Gurney's.

shortLabel: 'John Cheny' of the 1661 Braintree record = John Gurney
statement: The 'John Cheny' of the 1661 Braintree marriage and wife-death lines is John Gurney. The fair-copy manuscript reads 'John Girny, Senior' in ink, with 'Cheny' only a later pencil margin annotation that the 1886 print mistook for text; Pope 1900 independently ruled the printed Cheny a typographical error; no John Cheney family is otherwise attested at Braintree in 1661; and the surrounding facts fit Gurney — Mary Gurney's death three weeks earlier, the officiant Peter Brackett (a documented Gurney associate), and John Gurney's 1663 Braintree probate. Confidence is roughly 85-90%, the residual being the ambiguous deaths-page letterform.
